verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.71
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 3.71

verses.pali: 8. Ānandavagga
verses.english: 8. Ānanda

verses.pali: Channasutta
verses.english: With Channa

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

verses.pali: Atha kho channo paribbājako yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then the wanderer Channa went up to Venerable Ānanda and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho channo paribbājako āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Ānanda:

verses.pali: “tumhepi, āvuso ānanda, rāgassa pahānaṁ paññāpetha, dosassa pahānaṁ paññāpetha, mohassa pahānaṁ paññāpethā”ti.
verses.english: “Reverend Ānanda, do you advocate giving up greed, hate, and delusion?”

verses.pali: “Mayaṁ kho, āvuso, rāgassa pahānaṁ paññāpema, dosassa pahānaṁ paññāpema, mohassa pahānaṁ paññapemā”ti.
verses.english: “We do, reverend.”

verses.pali: “Kiṁ pana tumhe, āvuso, rāge ādīnavaṁ disvā rāgassa pahānaṁ paññāpetha, kiṁ dose ādīnavaṁ disvā dosassa pahānaṁ paññāpetha, kiṁ mohe ādīnavaṁ disvā mohassa pahānaṁ paññāpethā”ti?
verses.english: “But what drawbacks have you seen, Reverend Ānanda, that you advocate giving up greed, hate, and delusion?”

verses.pali: “Ratto kho, āvuso, rāgena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti;
verses.english: “A greedy person, overcome by greed, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They experience mental pain and sadness.

verses.pali: rāge pahīne nevattabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na cetasikaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
verses.english: When greed has been given up, they don’t intend to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They don’t experience mental pain and sadness.

verses.pali: Ratto kho, āvuso, rāgena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati;
verses.english: A greedy person does bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

verses.pali: rāge pahīne neva kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, na vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, na manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
verses.english: When greed has been given up, they don’t do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

verses.pali: Ratto kho, āvuso, rāgena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti;
verses.english: A greedy person doesn’t truly understand what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both.

verses.pali: rāge pahīne attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: When greed has been given up, they truly understand what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both.

verses.pali: Rāgo kho, āvuso, andhakaraṇo acakkhukaraṇo aññāṇakaraṇo paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṁvattaniko.
verses.english: Greed is a destroyer of sight, vision, and knowledge. It blocks wisdom, it’s on the side of distress, and it doesn’t lead to extinguishment.

verses.pali: Duṭṭho kho, āvuso, dosena …pe…
verses.english: A hateful person, overcome by hate, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. …

verses.pali: mūḷho kho, āvuso, mohena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti;
verses.english: A deluded person, overcome by delusion, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They experience mental pain and sadness.

verses.pali: mohe pahīne nevattabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na cetasikaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
verses.english: When delusion has been given up, they don’t intend to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They don’t experience mental pain and sadness.

verses.pali: Mūḷho kho, āvuso, mohena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati;
verses.english: A deluded person does bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

verses.pali: mohe pahīne neva kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, na vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, na manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
verses.english: When delusion has been given up, they don’t do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

verses.pali: Mūḷho kho, āvuso, mohena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti;
verses.english: A deluded person doesn’t truly understand what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both.

verses.pali: mohe pahīne attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: When delusion has been given up, they truly understand what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both.

verses.pali: Moho kho, āvuso, andhakaraṇo acakkhukaraṇo aññāṇakaraṇo paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṁvattaniko.
verses.english: Delusion is a destroyer of sight, vision, and knowledge; it blocks wisdom, it’s on the side of distress, and it doesn’t lead to extinguishment.

verses.pali: Idaṁ kho mayaṁ, āvuso, rāge ādīnavaṁ disvā rāgassa pahānaṁ paññāpema.
verses.english: This is the drawback we’ve seen in greed, hate, and delusion, and this is why we advocate giving them up.”

verses.pali: Idaṁ dose ādīnavaṁ disvā dosassa pahānaṁ paññāpema.
Idaṁ mohe ādīnavaṁ disvā mohassa pahānaṁ paññāpemā”ti.
“Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti?
verses.english: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion?”

verses.pali: “Atthāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti.
verses.english: “There is, reverend, a path and a practice for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion.”

verses.pali: “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti?
verses.english: “Well, what is it?”

verses.pali: “Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: “It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

verses.pali: sammādiṭṭhi …pe… sammāsamādhi.
verses.english: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṁ paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti.
verses.english: This is the path, this is the practice for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion.”

verses.pali: “Bhaddako kho, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāya.
verses.english: “This is a fine path, a fine practice, for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion.

verses.pali: Alañca panāvuso ānanda, appamādāyā”ti.
verses.english: Just this much is enough for diligence.”

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ.
